reasons: [reasoning_validity/major] D1 [CL2; criteriaAssessments C1 (assessment, weaknesses); counterarguments[3]; remainingUncertainty[0]] The draft misses an inference the packet supports directly. OpenANN-Bench ran Quiver 3.1 on 200M vectors (E6). That is twice the 2.x per-collection cap of 100M (E1), so Quiver must have held more than 100M vectors there, presumably in a 3.x sharded collection or in several collections. It still served filtered queries at 38 ms p95 with Recall@10 0.97 at 400 QPS. This is partial evidence that filtered search works above 100M, probably through sharding. Yet CL2 says 'The packet does not show whether Quiver's sharded collections fully support filters', C1 treats sharded filter and recall behaviour as entirely unknown, and the 'application-side sharding' counterargument is answered without this point. The correct statement is that the configuration is unknown, but 200M filtered at 0.97 recall is direct if partial evidence on the hard gate C1. The draft should state the inference and its caveat (the benchmark setup is undisclosed and may have used several collections), and the PoC should confirm how OpenANN configured Quiver.

findings: [minor/reviewer] D2 [practicalImplications[2] and practicalImplications[8]] The new hard requirement makes an engine fail if it misses p95 < 50 ms 'under concurrent writes'. Neither the request nor the packet gives a write rate (E10), and the pre-PoC step 'Define the team's recall target and filter selectivity distribution' leaves write and delete rates out. Without an agreed upsert/delete rate, that part of the elimination test cannot be applied consistently.

[minor/reviewer] D1 [practicalImplications[2] (decision rule); verdict ('Judge it with the pass/fail and weighted tie-break rule')] The new decision rule says 'If both pass, choose using the plan's criterion weights: C2 25, C1 20, C3 15, C4 15, C5 10, C6 8, C7 7', but it never says how each criterion is scored. There is no scale and no mapping from measured p95/recall/footprint to points. C1, C4 and C7 have also just been made pass/fail gates, so once both engines pass those gates their 42 points of weight cannot separate them, unless the draft says how a 'pass' is graded further. As written, two teams could apply the rule and reach different answers. The rule should state a scoring method, for example normalised measured values for C2, C3 and C5 and a 0-5 rubric for the others, or say which measured differences count as decisive.

[minor/reviewer] D3 [practicalImplications[2] (fallback sentence)] The new cut-down fallback is to 'run only the lowest-selectivity tier (about 1%) at about 300M, matched recall, on a sharded Quiver collection'. It names the Quiver configuration but not the matching Tessellate one (single collection, node count). It also does not say whether the C4 failover/upgrade drills and the concurrent-write test, both hard gates in the same rule, are kept or dropped. A cut-down PoC run this way could not apply the elimination rule just stated.
